To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the seroprevalance of rubella Ig-G antibody in pregnant women was high and not associated with age of the women, gestational age of the foetus, gravidity, education, occupation and vaccination.

the seroprevalance of rubella Ig G antibody in pregnant women attending antanatal clinic in LAUTECH Teaching Hospital Osogbo, was 87.5% and that it was not associated with any of the socio demographic factors studied.
the prevalence of rubella IgM and IgG antibodies in pregnant women in Osogbo was 2.5% and 87.5%, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the prevalence of rubella Ig G in the pregnant women in Osogbo and its environs.
the seroprevalance of Rubella virus in pregnant women in Osogbo.
the study of the seroprevalance of rubella Ig G antibody in pregnant women in Osogbo Nigeria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rubella IgG sero-survey among pregnant women in Osogbo is high and the study population is at risk of rubella infection.
there is a need for rubella vaccination for all women of reproductive age and children.
rubella vaccination should become part of national immunization programme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is high prevalence of rubella Ig G antibody in pregnant women in Osogbo.
rubella vaccination is not currently being provided to pregnant women in the studied population and this should be provided.
there is a need for routine rubella immunisation of children and pregnant women in Osogbo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rubella seroprevalences among pregnant women are high and that rubella vaccination should therefore be provided for all pregnant women and children.
rubella is a serious disease that can be prevented with vaccination.
there is need to implement a rubella vaccination campaign in Nigeria to prevent rubella infection during pregnancy.
